speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with a fever and altered mentation for two days; to help me understand the cause, have you experienced any recent head trauma, seizures, or exposure to tick bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.

Given your history of tics and use of haloperidol, combined with fever and altered mentation without other infectious symptoms, this presentation is classic for a reaction to antipsychotic medication. I will order blood tests to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, CK, and TSH.
